title: LLMs learn scientific taste from institutional traces across the social sciences

live_model.evidence: SI: 'Management base-architecture cells in ST13 (Qwen3-30B-A3B base 22.5%; Qwen3-4B base 26.7%; GPT-4.1-nano base 25.0%) ... first-token log-probability resolver'

prompt.location: Supplementary Methods 2 (SM2): pre-specified general social-science evaluation prompt; management expert-rubric prompt
prompt.note: Base controls used the general prompt zero-shot with a deterministic first-token log-probability resolver.

claim.location: Table ST13c, row Management, column Base accuracy

data.source: Benchmark pitches, labels and predictions in the reproducibility package github.com/FutureTech-OB/ai-taste (CC BY)

notes: Headline results are fine-tuned (SFT) GPT-4.1-nano (57.5% management) and need OpenAI fine-tuning; only the un-fine-tuned base control is Tier-B. Base accuracy is at chance (25%), so the claim is weak but checkable; the logprob resolver must be replicated.

resolution.plan: Take the 120 management pitches with tier labels from the CC BY reproducibility package named in the paper (github.com/FutureTech-OB/ai-taste); send the SM2 general evaluation prompt plus pitch to gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 with logprobs enabled and, at the first decoded token, softmax over the four tier tokens (exceptional, strong, fair, limited), argmax with the alphabetical tie-break of SM2; four-class accuracy vs 25.0% (ST13c, Management, Base).
resolution.approximation: Restricted-vocabulary first-token scoring is emulated through the chat API's top-k logprobs (tokens outside the top-k get zero mass); the value sits at chance, so agreement is weakly informative.
